completion_requirement: verdict=match and error_count=0 for every figure

figures.title: Companies plan to offer more benefits in five years.

errors.source_evidence: The source page shows a stacked bar chart with three vertical 100% bars (Small, Midsize, Large). Each bar is divided into Fewer benefits (light gray), About the same (dark gray) and More benefits (yellow). Segment labels sit inside the bars, the +7%/+6%/+5% change callouts sit beside the bars, and a legend sits at the bottom.
errors.html_evidence: The rendered HTML has no visual chart. It shows only a text legend line ("Legend: Fewer benefits; About the same; More benefits"), a bulleted list of change values, and a table. There are no bars, no stacked segments, and no colored legend swatches. The change callouts are detached from any bar.
errors.correction: Add a rendered stacked bar chart (SVG or CSS). It should have three bars labeled Small (10–99 employees), Midsize (100–999 employees) and Large (1,000 or more employees). Stack Fewer benefits (3%, 1%, 3%), About the same (40%, 35%, 30%) and More benefits (57%, 64%, 67%) in that order. Put the segment labels on the segments, place the +7%, +6% and +5% "change from 2023" callouts beside their bars, and add a legend with color swatches. Keep the data table beside the chart.

errors.source_evidence: In the source, the thin baseline sits directly under the bottoms of the three stacked bars. The category labels (Small, Midsize, Large and their employee ranges) sit below that line.
errors.html_evidence: In the render, the baseline (the .chart border-bottom) is drawn below the category labels, at about y=560. The bars end about 40px higher, at about y=521. The line therefore underlines the labels and almost touches the second label line (for example "(10–99 employees)"). The bars float above the axis.
errors.correction: Put the baseline directly under the bar bottoms, at the base of the .plot area, and place the category labels below it with clear spacing. Remove the border-bottom from the .chart container so the line no longer crowds or underlines the category text.
